plan.title: HFD vs chow mouse liver DE + hallmark GSEA
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq experiment: a 12,000 x 12 Salmon gene-level count matrix with mouse gene symbols (counts.csv) and a 12 x 2 sample table (metadata.csv) giving one condition per sample, 6 high-fat-diet vs 6 chow mice, unpaired. The research question has two parts — which genes change, and which hallmark pathways change — plus an explicit data-quality concern: sample_01 has a library size roughly 4x below the median.

The library-size caveat is handled first and empirically, not by assumption. Step T1S1 quantifies the depth imbalance, checks whether sample_01 is merely shallow (a size factor far from 1 but otherwise normal correlation/PCA behaviour, which DESeq2's median-of-ratios normalization absorbs) or genuinely aberrant (low gene detection, low correlation to its condition-mates, PCA outlier), and produces an explicit, evidence-based keep/exclude recommendation. It does not silently drop the sample: at n=6 per group, dropping one costs real power, so exclusion must be justified.

T1S2 runs the primary contrast, HFD vs chow, with DESeq2 on raw integer counts — the correct model for this design (negative binomial, unpaired two-group, ~condition, no batch term because the design is single-batch). It is run on all 12 samples as the primary result and, when T1S1 flagged sample_01, repeated without it as a pre-registered sensitivity analysis so the reader can see how much any conclusion depends on that one sample. LFC shrinkage (apeglm) gives ranking that is not dominated by low-count genes.

T1S3 takes the full shrunk-LFC ranking (not a thresholded gene list) into hallmark GSEA using the mouse MSigDB hallmark collection, which the reference store holds as MGI symbols — matching the identifier space of the counts matrix directly, so no ortholog mapping is needed and none should be invented. Ranking-based GSEA is chosen over over-representation because a 12,000-gene matrix with n=6/group may yield few genes past FDR 0.05, and hallmark ORA on a short list is underpowered. The step also reports concordance between the all-12 and drop-sample_01 rankings.

Acceptance criteria throughout demand the actual numbers (size factors, detected-gene counts, DE counts at stated thresholds, NES/padj per hallmark set) rather than narrative, and require that limitations — n=6/group, single batch so batch and diet are not separable, hallmark sets being mouse-ortholog-mapped — be stated rather than glossed.
